description: Tests that the stack depth skill correctly runs `loci analyse stack`, interprets the JSON envelope, and reports worst-case depth, call paths, per-function frames, warnings, and verdicts against a bound the user or the contract supplied. All functions are compiled into $LOCI_TEST_BLE_FRESH/basic_ble.out.
note: Set $LOCI_TEST_BLE_ROOT to your local BLE project root before running. Evals sd-5 and sd-6 instead use $LOCI_TEST_STALE_ROOT, a fixture run_evals.sh stages from evals/fixtures/stale-artifact/. It needs arm-none-eabi-gcc and a loci CLI with `build fresh`; without either, run_evals.sh skips them by detecting the unexpanded placeholder (there is no `requires` key to set — the placeholder itself is the gate, so a typo cannot bypass it). The fixture is deliberately UNINITIALIZED — no .loci/build.yaml — because that is the state every project is in for the length of the train-1 soak, and it is what makes the recipe provenance line's null branch reachable here. Staging a real recipe belongs to the Phase-4 eval rework (T14), when a CLI that can write one is everywhere.

evals.prompt: Analyze the stack depth for GAPBondMgr_ProcessEvent in $LOCI_TEST_BLE_FRESH/basic_ble.out. No stack budget — just show me the worst-case depth and the call path.
evals.expected_output: Runs `loci analyse stack` with --elf pointing to basic_ble.out and --entry-functions GAPBondMgr_ProcessEvent. Reports worst-case depth in bytes, the worst-case call path as a chain of function names, average depth, and per-function frame sizes along the worst path, then a conclusion table. Because the prompt named no budget and no contract bounds this function, it does NOT report a usage percentage or any pass-fail check against a threshold; a share of a figure this run measured (a frame as a percentage of the depth) is arithmetic on the run's own evidence and is allowed. GAPBondMgr_ProcessEvent's reach holds unresolved indirect-call sites, so the depth is a lower bound: the skill's lower-bound rule writes every figure as `≥<N> B`, the assessment is **Needs attention** with the indirect calls named — which composes to `CAUTION` on this uncontracted repo — and the verdict line closes as `Verdict: **CAUTION** — worst-case ≥<N> bytes, lower bound: <K> indirect call sites`, under the caption that no contract judged the run. A bare `PASS` is wrong because nothing bounded the depth and the figure is a floor; a `FAIL` is wrong because nothing was breached; the retired `○ cleared —` wire spelling never reaches the reader. Freshness: `loci build fresh` on this artifact may report `stale: null` (unknown) because sources named in its debug info are not on this machine; the freshness rule says to proceed on `null` and say so, quoting `.data.reason`, so a report that carries that caveat beside its `Artifact:` line is correct and complete, not hedged.

assertions.text: Response runs `loci analyse stack` with --elf pointing to basic_ble.out and --entry-functions GAPBondMgr_ProcessEvent
assertions.description: Must use the stack verb with the correct ELF and entry function

assertions.text: Response reports a worst-case depth in bytes (a specific number, not fabricated)
assertions.description: The core output: total accumulated stack bytes along the deepest path

assertions.text: Response shows a worst-case call path as a chain of function names (more than one function)
assertions.description: The path must show the actual chain from entry to deepest leaf

assertions.text: Response reports per-function frame sizes for functions along the worst path
assertions.description: Each function in the path should show its individual frame contribution

assertions.text: Response reports no usage percentage against a budget and no pass/fail check against a threshold, and closes on `CAUTION` as a lower bound — every figure in the verdict line carries `≥` and the line names the unresolved indirect calls as the cause — never on a bare PASS, a FAIL, or the retired `○ cleared` spelling
assertions.description: No bound was supplied by prompt or contract, so usage % and any pass/fail comparison must be absent. The depth is a floor (indirect calls in the function's reach), so the skill's lower-bound rule applies: Needs attention with the cause named, composed to CAUTION on a repo with no contract. A frame stated as a share of the measured depth is not a budget percentage

evals.prompt: Run stack depth analysis on GAPBondMgr_ProcessEvent in $LOCI_TEST_BLE_FRESH/basic_ble.out. Keep it under 768 bytes.
evals.expected_output: Runs `loci analyse stack` with --elf and --entry-functions, and WITHOUT --stack-budget: the request's figure is the skill's own to compare, never the wheel's banded flag. Reports worst-case depth, usage as a percentage of 768 bytes, and a PASS or FAIL verdict against 768 bytes. The 768 is a bound the user stated in the request, which is one of the two sources that reach a measured verdict, so judging against it is correct; the report quotes the figure back and says it came from the request. The percentage is the measured depth over 768 — about 125% here — and it carries a `≥` (`≥125%`) because unresolved indirect calls in the function's reach make the depth a lower bound; the verdict is FAIL. It must NOT invent a further band inside that bound, such as treating 50% or 80% of 768 as a caution line. Also reports the worst-case path and per-function frames. Freshness: `loci build fresh` on this artifact may report `stale: null` (unknown) because sources named in its debug info are not on this machine; the freshness rule says to proceed on `null` and say so, quoting `.data.reason`, so a report that carries that caveat beside its `Artifact:` line is correct and complete, not hedged.

assertions.text: Response judges the measured depth against 768 bytes and attributes that bound to the request
assertions.description: A bound stated in the request is the user's own, so it reaches a measured verdict

assertions.text: Response reports usage as a percentage of the 768-byte budget (about 125%, written `≥125%` since the depth is a lower bound)
assertions.description: Usage percentage is required when a bound supplies the denominator; the request's figure is one. Stating only the overage in bytes does not meet this

assertions.text: Response includes a PASS or FAIL verdict against 768 bytes, with no additional percentage band inside it
assertions.description: The verdict compares worst-case depth against the stated 768 bytes. Treating a fraction of 768 as a caution line would be a skill-invented band and is wrong

assertions.text: Response shows the worst-case call path and per-function frame sizes
assertions.description: Full reporting is still required alongside the verdict

evals.prompt: Analyze stack depth for all root functions in $LOCI_TEST_BLE_FRESH/basic_ble.out. Don't specify entry functions — let the tool auto-detect them.
evals.expected_output: Runs `loci analyse stack` with --elf but without --entry-functions, letting the verb walk the binary's own roots. Reports per-function results for multiple entry points, each with worst-case depth, path, and frame sizes. Freshness: `loci build fresh` on this artifact may report `stale: null` (unknown) because sources named in its debug info are not on this machine; the freshness rule says to proceed on `null` and say so, quoting `.data.reason`, so a report that carries that caveat beside its `Artifact:` line is correct and complete, not hedged.

assertions.text: Response runs `loci analyse stack` without --entry-functions to auto-detect roots
assertions.description: Auto-detection mode should be used when no entry functions are specified

assertions.text: Response reports results for more than one function
assertions.description: A real ELF has multiple root functions; the tool should find and report them

assertions.text: Each reported function has a worst-case depth and path
assertions.description: Per-function reporting is required even in multi-function mode

evals.prompt: Analyze stack depth for osal_msg_send in $LOCI_TEST_BLE_FRESH/basic_ble.out. I suspect there may be recursive calls in the chain. Use --max-recursion-depth 3.
evals.expected_output: Runs `loci analyse stack` with --entry-functions osal_msg_send and --max-recursion-depth 3. If recursion is detected, reports a warning about the recursive call and notes the depth is bounded to 3 iterations. If no recursion is found, reports the depth normally. Either way, the tool should handle the flag and report clearly. Freshness: `loci build fresh` on this artifact may report `stale: null` (unknown) because sources named in its debug info are not on this machine; the freshness rule says to proceed on `null` and say so, quoting `.data.reason`, so a report that carries that caveat beside its `Artifact:` line is correct and complete, not hedged.

assertions.text: Response runs `loci analyse stack` with --max-recursion-depth 3
assertions.description: The recursion depth flag must be passed through

assertions.text: Response reports the worst-case depth and path for osal_msg_send
assertions.description: Core analysis must complete regardless of recursion

assertions.text: If recursion is detected, response mentions it explicitly as a warning
assertions.description: Recursion warnings are critical for stack safety — they must be surfaced

evals.prompt: I just changed kernel_main in $LOCI_TEST_STALE_ROOT/blink.c to call a new build_pattern() helper. Give me the worst-case stack depth for kernel_main against a 2048-byte budget. The project builds with `make` from $LOCI_TEST_STALE_ROOT (its Makefile links kernel.elf with arm-none-eabi-gcc).
evals.expected_output: The stale-selection regression, on a project a recipe governs: `.loci/build.yaml` records `build.system: make`, `full_build: make -C <root>`, `artifacts.elf: kernel.elf`, target armv6-m, validated compile-check. The tree contains kernel.elf linked BEFORE the edit (225 s older than blink.c; it does not contain build_pattern or render_frame at all) plus a post-edit object under .loci/build/objects/armv6-m/. The skill lets the CLI's freshness ladder refuse kernel.elf (`loci analyse stack` refuses the stale binary and falls to the object, `via: ranked`) and must NOT report numbers from kernel.elf. On the object `worst_case_depth` is not a depth — the unapplied R_ARM_THM_CALL relocation loses the call edge, so kernel_main reads as 8 B — so the report gives at most the 8 B own frame, labelled as such, and no depth, no percentage of the 2048-byte budget and no PASS against it. The rebuild is the user's: the envelope says `before_saved: false` with `before_reason: no_edit_this_turn`, and the house rules' relink rule for that case is to ask once — naming the refused kernel.elf and the recipe's own build, `make` (its `full_build`) — and run it only on a yes. In this single-turn eval no answer arrives, so the correct response carries that question or offer — anywhere in it: before or after the conclusion table and footer, the house rule is about asking, not about ordering — with the stale ELF refused and no depth measured in its place as the answer. Saying that a relink loses no baseline is correct, because `no_edit_this_turn` means exactly that; a `CAUTION` close saying the depth could not be judged against the budget is correct too. It never runs `make` unasked, never hand-types a link into LOCI's own build directory, never edits the recipe, and never presents a ranked list of candidate binaries. It carries the mandatory `Artifact:` line naming what was measured (the object, own-frame scope) and the `Recipe:` line beside it — `.loci/build.yaml`, target armv6-m, validated compile-check — not a `null` and not an invented path. The staged recipe was written by `loci init` and never confirmed (`confirmed_by_user: false`), so the line correctly carries the skill's qualifier `not confirmed by anyone` with `/loci:init` as what clears it, and the envelope's recipe warning is relayed beside it: that is the fixture's real state, not an invention. sd-6 is the same fixture WITH the user's yes in the prompt, and grades the rebuilt numbers (3120 B, 152%, FAIL). A run that reports 0.4% PASS (the stale ELF), 8 B PASS against the budget (the bare .o taken as a depth), or that relinks unasked or by hand, is a FAIL of this eval.

assertions.text: Response lets the CLI's freshness check run before reporting numbers — `loci analyse stack` (whose ladder refuses a stale artifact) or `loci build fresh --elf` — rather than reading numbers off kernel.elf directly
assertions.description: The gate must run at all; this is the defect the tester reported

assertions.text: Response identifies kernel.elf as stale / older than blink.c, and does NOT present its numbers as the answer
assertions.description: Detecting staleness but reporting the stale numbers anyway is still the bug

assertions.text: Response does not present the object's `worst_case_depth` as a depth: at most the 8 B own frame, labelled own-frame / object scope, with no percentage of the 2048-byte budget and no PASS verdict against it
assertions.description: A relocatable .o loses cross-call edges, so taken as a depth it reports 8 B / PASS: fresh artifact, confidently wrong answer

assertions.text: Response names the recipe's recorded build, `make` (its `full_build`), as the relink that would make kernel.elf measurable, and asks for it or offers it as the user's step rather than running it unasked
assertions.description: before_saved is false with reason no_edit_this_turn, so the house rules' relink rule is: ask once, run on a yes. Under `claude -p` / `copilot -p` the question tool cannot be answered and no yes arrives, so the response carries the question or the offer, wherever it places it — after the conclusion table and footer is fine. A plain next step handed to the user (`make -C <root>`, then re-run) satisfies this exactly as a yes/no question does, and 'relinking loses no baseline' is correct beside the question or offer, not instead of it (that is what no_edit_this_turn means); what fails it is running make, or linking by hand

assertions.text: Response does not run `make` unasked, does not link a binary by hand into .loci/build/, and does not edit the recipe
assertions.description: The project's own build is the only rebuild, and it is the user's to approve; a hand-linked binary under LOCI's own directory has no provenance behind it

assertions.text: Response includes an `Artifact:` provenance line naming which binary was measured (the object, own-frame scope) and when it was built
assertions.description: The durable safety net: even if selection regresses, the reader can see what was measured

assertions.text: Response does not present a ranked list of candidate artifacts it searched for
assertions.description: The recipe replaced candidate collection and provenance ranking with one recorded artifact. A response that reasons about which of several binaries to prefer is running the deleted flow

assertions.text: Response carries the `Recipe:` provenance line beside `Artifact:`, naming `.loci/build.yaml` with target armv6-m and its validation tier (`validated compile-check`), and does not print `null` or an invented path; the qualifier `not confirmed by anyone` is correct here, because the staged recipe is unconfirmed
assertions.description: Every absolute report names the recipe its numbers rest on; this tree has one, so prose saying it has none is as wrong as a fabricated path. The staging init writes the recipe with confirmed_by_user false, so the skill's confirmation qualifier and the relayed recipe warning are the fixture's state, not fabrication

evals.prompt: Run a stack depth analysis on kernel_main in $LOCI_TEST_STALE_ROOT with a stack budget of 2048 bytes. kernel.elf there may be out of date — if it is, rebuild it the way the project builds before you measure.
evals.expected_output: The frame-sizing half of the regression, on a project a recipe governs: `.loci/build.yaml` records `build.system: make`, `full_build: make -C <root>`, `artifacts.elf: kernel.elf`. kernel.elf is stale (225 s older than blink.c), so the CLI's freshness check refuses it; the response rebuilds the way the recipe records — `make`, the recipe's `full_build` — and measures the rebuilt kernel.elf, the recipe's own artifact, rather than linking a binary of its own into LOCI's build directory. kernel_main reaches a 3072-byte stack buffer through build_pattern; frame sizes are kernel_main 8, build_pattern 3088, render_frame 24 (gcc -fstack-usage agrees), so the worst case is 3120 bytes: 152.3% of the 2048-byte budget, verdict FAIL, path kernel_main -> build_pattern -> render_frame, largest frame build_pattern at ~99% of the total. Before asmslicer 1.1.1, compute_frame_size matched decimal-only immediates while capstone renders >= 10 in hex, so every frame collapsed to ~8 bytes and this exact case reported 16 B / 0.8% / PASS. Any PASS verdict, or a worst case anywhere near 8-24 bytes, is a FAIL of this eval.

assertions.text: Response reports a worst-case depth of 3120 bytes for kernel_main (not ~8, ~16 or ~24)
assertions.description: A near-zero figure means frame sizing regressed to the decimal-immediate bug

assertions.text: Response reports a FAIL verdict against the 2048-byte budget at roughly 152% usage
assertions.description: The budget verdict must be FAIL — the code overflows the budget by 2x

assertions.text: Response identifies build_pattern as the dominant frame at about 3088 bytes
assertions.description: The 3072-byte buffer plus 16 bytes of prologue; it is 99% of the worst path

assertions.text: Response reports the worst-case path as kernel_main -> build_pattern -> render_frame
assertions.description: All three frames must be summed along the path, not just the entry frame

assertions.text: Response rebuilds the stale kernel.elf through the project's own build (`make`, the recipe's `full_build`) and measures kernel.elf — not a binary it linked itself into .loci/build/objects/
assertions.description: The recipe records how this project builds; a hand-linked binary under LOCI's own directory has no provenance behind it

assertions.text: Response includes an `Artifact:` provenance line naming which binary was measured and when it was built
assertions.description: Mandatory for every absolute report, fresh artifact or not

assertions.text: Response carries the `Recipe:` provenance line beside `Artifact:`, naming `.loci/build.yaml` with target armv6-m and its validation tier (`validated compile-check`), and does not print `null` or an invented path; the qualifier `not confirmed by anyone` is correct here, because the staged recipe is unconfirmed
assertions.description: Every absolute report names the recipe its numbers rest on; this tree has one. The staging init writes it with confirmed_by_user false, so the skill's confirmation qualifier (with /loci:init as what clears it) is the fixture's state, not fabrication

evals.prompt: What's the worst-case stack depth of this image? $LOCI_TEST_BLE_FRESH/basic_ble.out
evals.expected_output: Runs `loci analyse stack` once with --elf and WITHOUT --entry-functions: the user named no roots, so the verb walks the binary's own roots (every function nothing calls) beside any contract functions, and `data.detail.roots` reads `binary`. Reports the deepest function in `data.detail.stack_analysis` as the image's worst case -- its depth in bytes and its worst-case path -- not the depth of one function a contract entry happens to name. The footer's N is `summary.total_functions_analyzed`, the roots walked (hundreds on this image), never 1. With indirect-call sites in the roots' reach the depth is a lower bound and every figure takes a `>=` with the cause named. Does not run `loci elf stack`.

assertions.text: Response's one analysis call passes no --entry-functions
assertions.description: The user named no roots, so the binary's own roots are walked (AAD-7619)

assertions.text: Response reports the deepest reported function's depth and its worst-case path as the image's worst case
assertions.description: The whole-image question is answered from the deepest root, not from a contract's function

assertions.text: Response's footer N is the count of roots walked (summary.total_functions_analyzed), not 1
assertions.description: N is every root walked; a 1 is the collapsed sample the ticket reports

assertions.text: Response does not run loci elf stack
assertions.description: The envelope carries the figures; the elf verbs are not this skill's to call
